solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Student leaves cougar for one old lady

indicators.note: the student walks out of the word, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a cougar is an example of a mammal
L is the learner-driver plate, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A student abandons a big cat in exchange for an elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' signals that the cougar is only an example of a larger class, the mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: Old lady is informal slang for a mother, and this is a childish word for mother.

clue.text: Set of stories strangely gloomy about unknown time with husband

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the other pieces
strangely means the letters come out in an unusual arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A collection of tales oddly depressing about some indeterminate era with a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges GLOOMY as MOLOGY, which goes 'about' YTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythology is the body of myths belonging to a culture, a collection of traditional tales.

clue.text: Concubine loses son three times in joint

indicators.note: the concubine word gives up the stated letters

parts.note: a mistress is a kept woman, a concubine
S for son, taken three times over

explanation.surface: A kept woman parts with her son on three occasions at a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: MISTRESS has three Ss; removing all of them leaves MITRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is a carpentry joint where two pieces meet at an angle, as at a picture frame corner.

clue.text: What's grown from fuss surrounding unfinished oral

indicators.note: the fuss word goes around the other piece

parts.note: ado means fuss

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is left off

parts.note: vocal means spoken, oral

explanation.surface: A query about what results when a fuss envelops an incomplete spoken exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's grown' reads like a question about growth, but it simply defines a cultivated fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An avocado is a fruit grown on trees, so the definition fits as something produced by cultivation.

clue.text: Revolutionary ops began working on gallon waterproof container

indicators.note: revolutionary letters are overturned and thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Radical operations get going on a waterproof bag that holds a gallon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' shuffles OPS BEGAN into SPONGEBA; 'working on' simply joins it to G for gallon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge bag is a small waterproof pouch for carrying toiletries when travelling.

clue.text: Sturgeon's cross, avoiding Liberal lampoonery

indicators.note: the cross word avoids, so omits, the stated letter

parts.note: the saltire is Scotland's flag, the cross of Nicola Sturgeon, former Scottish First Minister

explanation.surface: A Scottish leader's annoyance at keeping clear of mockery by a Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective for angry, but it is the saltire, the diagonal cross on Scotland's flag, linked to Nicola Sturgeon, the former Scottish leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is ridicule used to expose folly, much the same thing as lampooning.

clue.text: Succeed at the long jump away from home?

definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: to bound further than others, to out-jump them

explanation.surface: An athlete hopes to win the long jump at an away meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Outbound describes travel heading away from home, and read playfully it means jumping further than rivals.

clue.text: Sparkle of good settled theory now and then

parts.note: lit means alighted or settled, as a bird does

indicators.note: only every other letter of theory is kept

explanation.surface: The brilliance of a sound, established theory shows only occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitter is a sparkling light, so the two words name the same shimmering effect.

clue.text: Broadcast supporting set welcoming hospital's invalid transport

indicators.note: in a down answer, the batch word sits above and supports the broadcast word
the set word takes the hospital letter inside it

parts.note: a batch is a set or group
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A broadcast backing a TV set takes in hospital transport for the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' is the noun for an ill person, not the adjective meaning void. Upper-class spa town Bath gave its name to this wheeled chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath chair is an old hooded wheelchair used to carry an invalid, so it is transport for the infirm.

clue.text: Frenchman possibly with house for a revolting person

indicators.note: with joins the house letters to the Frenchman word as a replacement
for says the house letters stand in place of the letter a

parts.note: a Gaul is an ancient inhabitant of France, so a Frenchman by example

explanation.surface: A Frenchman, perhaps, swapping a house for a disgusting individual.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghoul is someone with a morbid, repulsive interest in death, a revolting type.

clue.text: Twerp wanting to have old rag hat

parts.note: a tit is slang for a foolish person, a twerp
to be for something is to be in favour of it, wanting it
tat is shabby old cloth or junk

explanation.surface: A silly person longs to own an old rag of a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is Cockney rhyming slang: the phrase rhymes with hat and means a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang this tit-for-tat phrase, rhyming with hat, stands for a hat, often shortened to titfer.

clue.text: Begin digging around river

definitions.note: a verb in the clue, standing in for the noun meaning a beginning

indicators.note: the keen word is placed around the river letter

parts.note: if you dig something you are into it, keen on it

explanation.surface: A command to start excavating near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digging' looks like spadework but is slang for liking, giving INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction is the beginning of something, such as the opening bars of a song.

clue.text: Ordinary enclosure, dry out of doors

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
a pen is an enclosure for animals
to air laundry is to dry it out

explanation.surface: An ordinary pen, kept dry, sits outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taking place outside, rather than within a building, is said to happen in the fresh outdoor air.

clue.text: Visual's up to date, putting operator first

indicators.note: putting, completed by first, moves the operator letters within the word
first says the operator letters go to the very start of the word

parts.note: topical means current, up to date

explanation.surface: A visual display is current, with the operator given priority.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Visual is just 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to sight or vision, so it matches visual as an adjective.

clue.text: Schoolmate sadly abandoning scruffy sham fur

indicators.note: sadly here means badly, so the letters of the schoolmate are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written: its letters are the pool
taken as written: these letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A school friend is upset at giving up a shabby imitation fur.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: SCHOOLMATE holds the letters of SHAM plus the answer; 'abandoning' removes SHAM and 'scruffy' also signals that the remaining letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat of the Americas whose pelt was prized as a fur.

clue.text: Create surface cover, set up and talk at length; vanish

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means the word is written upwards

parts.note: to pave is to lay a hard surface over ground
to orate is to make a long speech

explanation.surface: Lay a road, get up and make a long speech, then disappear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns PAVE into EVAP in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to turn to vapour and so disappear, hence to vanish.

clue.text: With limits of barrier removed, fish intrude beyond boundaries

indicators.note: limits of points to the outer letters at each edge of the barrier word
removed says those outer edge letters are taken away from the barrier word

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Once the edges of a barrier go, fish stray beyond their bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intrude' alone looks like the definition, but 'beyond boundaries' belongs with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to advance gradually past the proper limits onto someone else's territory.

clue.text: Awfully cheeky and unoriginal

indicators.note: awfully means very badly, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something terribly impudent and lacking originality.
explanation.walkthrough: The little link word that seems to join two definitions is really part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed means overused and trite, so stale and unoriginal.

clue.text: Brisker steed initially more excitable

indicators.note: only the first letter of steed is taken

parts.note: nappy is a term for a skittish, excitable horse, so nappier is more excitable

explanation.surface: A faster horse begins more frisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Nappy is a horse-racing term for a highly strung horse, unrelated to babies.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappier means quicker and livelier, the same as brisker.

clue.text: Yen — yen! Making money

parts.note: Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen currency
earning is making money

explanation.surface: A longing for Japanese currency, the way to get rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word plays both senses: the first yen is a craving, the second is the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A yen is a strong desire or longing, the same sense as a deep craving.

clue.text: Benefactor promoting new American centre

indicators.note: in a down answer, promoting moves the new letter higher, earlier in the word

parts.note: an uncle is a generous relative, a benefactor

explanation.surface: A donor sponsors a new centre in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' lifts the N of UNCLE one place to give NUCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central core of something, around which the rest gathers.

clue.text: Material's marvellous, almost sumptuous

parts.note: fab is informal for fabulous, marvellous

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: rich means sumptuous, luxurious

explanation.surface: A cloth that is wonderful and very nearly luxurious.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth or textile, the stuff garments are made of, which is material.

clue.text: I will follow hound that hunts for money

indicators.note: the I comes after the hound in the answer

parts.note: the Afghan is a breed of hunting hound

explanation.surface: I will go after a hunting dog in pursuit of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The afghani is the currency of Afghanistan, so it is a form of money.

clue.text: Not hopeful result of adding selection of oriental foods

parts.note: dim prospects are not hopeful
a sum is the total from adding

explanation.surface: A pessimistic total from adding up a Chinese meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum is a Cantonese meal of many small dumplings and snacks served as an assortment.

clue.text: Succeeded, as things are, to halt flow from peak

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
now means at present, as things are
to cap a well or pipe is to seal it and halt its flow

explanation.surface: Something succeeded, for the present, in stopping water running off a mountain top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from peak' frames the definition loosely: the answer is the white covering found on a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowcap is the layer of snow crowning a mountain peak, standing here for the peak itself.

clue.text: Outdated second squad

parts.note: a team is a squad

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned reserve squad.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is used adjectivally for old-fashioned technology, as in steam radio, hence outdated.

clue.text: Part of maturing row not developed towards centre

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of a ripening line of crops failed to grow inwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrown describes something that has grown inward, into the flesh, like a toenail turning towards the middle.

clue.text: Month to go over nearly everything to do with numbering system

parts.note: OCT is the abbreviation for October

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, so its final letter is cut

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A month to review almost everything about a number system.
explanation.definitionFit: Octal describes the base-eight method of counting, so it relates to a numbering system.

clue.text: Blot out absence of effort over beginning of resits

indicators.note: the first letter of resits is put in, covered over by the other word

parts.note: ease is the absence of effort

indicators.note: the opening letter of resits is taken

explanation.surface: A student wants to wipe out the lazy approach before the first retakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or obliterate, the sense of blotting something out.

clue.text: With no hesitation saintly and not heartless in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed and set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the middle letter of not is cut out

parts.note: taken as written before its heart goes

explanation.surface: Without pausing, a good person and a cold one get into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the O from NOT, leaving NT; 'in trouble' shuffles SAINTLY with NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something instantly means doing it at once, without any delay or hesitation.

clue.text: Turmoil as postal system reported awful storm

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the postal word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the mail is the postal system

indicators.note: an awful arrangement of the letters jumbles them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Chaos as the post is said to have suffered a terrible storm.
explanation.walkthrough: MAEL is pronounced like MAIL; 'awful' rearranges STORM into STROM.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is literally a violent whirlpool and figuratively a state of great confusion.

clue.text: Avoided work and moved along, ignoring leader

indicators.note: the first letter, the leader, is left out of the word

parts.note: sidled means moved along furtively, sideways

explanation.surface: Someone shirked and edged along without the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to do nothing useful, to loaf rather than get on with a job.
